question: What is the primary focus of community health compared to individual clinical care?

options.A: A specific localized group of people
options.B: Only the surgical patients in a ward
options.C: One patient inside a hospital ward
options.D: The financial profit of health clinics

explanation: Community health specifically targets populations within a defined area rather than isolated individuals. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T1#GNS225_U2_T1_h1)

question: How does the World Health Organization define health?

options.A: The total absence of any infectious disease
options.B: Having normal blood pressure and temperature
options.C: Complete physical, mental, and social well-being
options.D: Being able to work without taking hospital leave

explanation: Health encompasses a broad state of well-being rather than just lacking physical symptoms. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T1#GNS225_U2_T1_h1)

question: An aggregate of people sharing common personal or environmental characteristics is called a what?
explanation: A population represents a broad collection of people sharing defined traits or living spaces. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T1#GNS225_U2_T1_h2)

question: Which term describes groups facing higher health risks due to socioeconomic disadvantages?
explanation: Vulnerable groups experience disproportionate health risks caused by systemic social and economic hurdles. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T1#GNS225_U2_T1_h2)

question: Routine childhood immunization against measles is an example of which level of prevention?
explanation: Primary prevention stops diseases from occurring in the first place through vaccines and health promotion. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T1#GNS225_U2_T1_h3)

question: A community blood pressure screening camp at a market square represents what type of prevention?
explanation: Screening aims at early detection and prompt intervention for conditions already present in an individual. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T1#GNS225_U2_T1_h3)

question: What does PHC stand for in community health nursing practice?
explanation: PHC stands for Primary Health Care, the core strategy for delivering accessible community-level services. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T1#GNS225_U2_T1_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of conducting a community diagnosis?

options.A: To identify local health problems and plan interventions
options.B: To punish people who refuse to build pit latrines
options.C: To test new experimental drugs without ethical review
options.D: To generate revenue for the local government council

explanation: Community diagnosis uncovers prevalent health issues so nurses and leaders can prioritize correct solutions. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T1#GNS225_U2_T1_h4)

question: The total number of existing disease cases in a population at a specific time is known as what?
explanation: Prevalence counts all existing cases at a snapshot in time, unlike incidence which counts only brand-new cases. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T1#GNS225_U2_T1_h5)

question: A sudden outbreak of cholera cases in a local village exceeding normal expectations is called a what?
explanation: An epidemic describes a sudden surge of disease cases well above normal baseline levels in a community. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T1#GNS225_U2_T1_h5)

question: What term describes individuals or groups with a vested interest in a health program?
explanation: Stakeholders encompass anyone impacted by or invested in the outcomes of a health initiative. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T1#GNS225_U2_T1_h6)

question: Why is program sustainability an important goal for community health nurses?

options.A: It stops patients from visiting private hospitals
options.B: It ensures services continue after donor funding stops
options.C: It removes the need for community participation
options.D: It guarantees automatic promotion for local staff

explanation: Sustainable programs outlast short-term grants by building local capacity and self-reliance. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T1#GNS225_U2_T1_h6)
